decision.explanation: The line's direction vector is B-A=⟨-1,5,-1⟩, which is normal to the plane. Its dot product with Q is -1+5(-4)-2=-23, so the plane is r·⟨-1,5,-1⟩=-23.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(1,-4,2)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(2,1,-3)$ and $B(1,6,-4).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨1,-4,2⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(2,1,-3)$ and $B(1,6,-4)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,6,-4⟩-⟨2,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,5,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-1,5,-1⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ & =⟨1,-4,2⟩\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ & =-23.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(1,-4,2)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(2,1,-3)$ and $B(1,6,-4).$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨1,-4,2⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(2,1,-3)$ and $B(1,6,-4)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,6,-4⟩-⟨2,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,5,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-1,5,-1⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ & =⟨1,-4,2⟩\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ & =-23.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,b,\,0⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩=-14.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
after.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩=-14$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨6,-2,0⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩ & =0 \\ 6{t}_{1}-2{t}_{2} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =3{t}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},3{t}_{1},{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the third component of $v$ eqauls $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{3}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{1}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{1}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{3}.$

after.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(4,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(-1,0,1)$ and $B(1,0,-1).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨4,-2,3⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(-1,0,1)$ and $B(1,0,-1)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,0,-1⟩-⟨-1,0,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,0,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨2,0,-2⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,-2⟩ & =⟨4,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,-2⟩ & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(4,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(-1,0,1)$ and $B(1,0,-1).$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨4,-2,3⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(-1,0,1)$ and $B(1,0,-1)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,0,-1⟩-⟨-1,0,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,0,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨2,0,-2⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,-2⟩ & =⟨4,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,-2⟩ & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩=\sqrt{2}.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩=\sqrt{2}$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨3,2,-1⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩ & =0 \\ 3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}-{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{3} & =3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,{t}_{2},\,3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{2}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{2}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{2}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{1}{2}.$

content.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩=\sqrt{2}.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
content.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩=\sqrt{2}$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨3,2,-1⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩ & =0 \\ 3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}-{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{3} & =3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,{t}_{2},\,3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{2}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{2}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{2}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{1}{2}.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(-3,0,2)$ and $B(2,1,3)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨2,1,3⟩-⟨-3,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨5,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨5,1,1⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ & =⟨3,-2,5⟩\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,-2,5)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(-3,0,2)$ and $B(2,1,3).$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,-2,5⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(-3,0,2)$ and $B(2,1,3)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨2,1,3⟩-⟨-3,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨5,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨5,1,1⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ & =⟨3,-2,5⟩\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
